Add some chaos to your routine.

No one ever improves by staying in their room in front of a computer for years.

Something to think about

A lot of SaaS founders are constantly looking for more traffic.

But if you already have hundreds of people coming to your product every month, acquisition might not be your biggest problem anymore.

Look at what happens after:

How many create an account?
How many actually reach the value of the product?
How many come back a few days later?
How many eventually pay?

Adding more traffic to a leaky funnel doesn’t fix the problem.

Before trying to get 1,000 more visitors, try to understand what’s actually happening inside your product.

If your SaaS is making money today but you're still using Resend for your emails, there's a problem somewhere.

The real problem is that you're treating your emails as just events in your code.

API calls scattered everywhere, cron jobs handling the logic, conditions all over the place, etc.

Resend itself isn't really the problem here.

The real problem is the lack of coherence.

Let me explain:

When your SaaS starts generating revenue, you should be able to see your emails, understand why they're being sent, edit your sequences, measure their performance, and improve them without touching 15 different places in your code.

You need to optimize, understand what's happening, and actually build a high-performing system.

Emails aren't only there to make you more money.

They're also there to help you understand your ICP better, provide value, build relationships, and create a better experience.

And I know some people won't like this, but using Resend forever is kind of lazy haha.

If your SaaS is making money, you need to start taking this part seriously.

Right now, I’m working on a Hermes agent connected to Stepers’ distribution

The goal is simple:

Help me understand what actually drives traffic to Stepers and what I should do more of.

Every day, the agent analyzes my posts, compares them with traffic on the landing page, looks for patterns I might miss, and stores the important signals in a database.

So instead of looking at impressions, likes or traffic separately, I can start answering questions like:

Which topics actually bring people to the product?

Which posts generate interest but no traffic?

Which formats should I double down on?

What changed compared to the previous week?

Then every weekend, it creates a complete PDF report and sends it to me by email with what worked, the patterns it found, and what I should focus on the following week.

Basically, I’m trying to turn my distribution data into actual decisions instead of just more dashboards.

If you have a SaaS, I think this is the kind of tool that could really help you. 

If you’re interested in this kind of thing, comment “TOOL” and follow me, and I’ll share a playbook on how to build this agent.

Most SaaS products that make money have understood something many SaaS founders still underestimate.

There’s a moment when a user truly understands the value of the product in front of them.

That’s what people usually call the “aha moment,” even though I’m not a huge fan of that expression ahaha.

In practice, it’s an action they take or a result they get that makes them think:

“Ok, now I understand why this product can actually help me.”

So your goal is simple:

How do you make your user experience that moment within the first few minutes?

Momentum is built. It comes from the effort you put in every single day.

One step at a time, the snowball gets bigger and bigger.

When you feel yourself gaining momentum, moving faster, and things starting to accelerate for you...

Don’t stop.

To do more, you need to do less.
It might sound weird ahaha, but it’s true.

When you’re a solo founder, you’re everywhere at once: working on the product, distribution, talking to people, coding, etc.

What I’ve noticed is that this approach can become a problem.

You switch tasks eight times a day, try to do everything at once, and your attention gets diluted.

In the end, you make progress in a lot of different directions, but at best, it’s average.

That’s also why people often say to focus on one channel and one feature at a time.

And on a daily basis, focus on THE task that will generate 80% of the results.

Today, what is the one task that, if completed, would give you 80% of the results and move you forward massively?

That’s the kind of question I try to ask myself every day to make sure I’m working on the real priority and not spreading myself too thin.
Being mentally obese means constantly consuming more and more information every day just to avoid doing what actually matters: Taking action.

If I told you that you were 30 failures away from achieving your goals, how fast would you move?

Someone once told me this sentence and it completely changed the way I think, since then I’ve committed to ONE thing, stop being slow, stop this disguised procrastination.

That’s why this month of September is going to be essential for Stepers, because my goal is to make the project real with an actual usable version and some MRR.

And I hope you have the same mindset for your own project.

Because in reality, when you choose a path, a direction in life, either you go all in or you do nothing at all and I think this mindset of setting big short-term goals and trying to move as fast as possible is something extremely beneficial.

You can see it as sprint periods, after that you can rest if you want to.

And you, what mindset do you try to keep in your head every day to reach your goals?

I generated my first SaaS revenue thanks to a simple email and yet, for months, I had completely underestimated this channel and you probably do too.

On my previous project, I sent an email to my users with a simple offer:

My product, for life, for €50, an irresistible offer in a well-written and well-branded email and a few hours later, I received a Stripe notification.

Someone had bought it, someone who had never pulled out their credit card before.

I could barely believe it ahaha, it was the first entrepreneurial revenue I had ever made in my life and I didn’t really know how to react so I started jumping around everywhere.

But from that moment on, I decided I was going to put a much more serious email strategy in place.

Not just to sell.

But to send the right message at the right moment:

→ Bring an inactive user back
→ Help them reach their first result
→ Reduce churn
→ Increase LTV
→ Convert a trial into a paying customer

Whether you have 10, 100 or 1,000 users, emails remain an important part of your SaaS.

The objective changes, that’s all, when you have 10 users you don’t send the same type of emails as when you have 2,000.

But their importance stays the same.

That’s exactly what I’m working on with Stepers:

Making this whole strategy much simpler.

Knowing what to send, to whom, and at what moment.

Because in the end, that’s what really matters.

Reduce churn
Increase conversion
